chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Playing to fit the singer's mood
summary: McRae says he accompanied Ella, Cab and Dinah Washington by fitting the mood, not showing off.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: He say, "(Inaudible), we gonna play (inaudible). What you and Cobbs gonna do. What do you wanna do?" So I say, "That gives us an idea," you know. Give me an idea. Because this the way I worked with Chick. We always worked our things out, you know. You gonna do a stage show, you gonna do something on it, you work it out, you know. If I was gonna play something behind Cab, I wouldn't get up there and just play things just to show myself. I'd play -- I used to play -- When Cab used to be down front, and I'd come in behind him. And sometime I'd play some melody, something behind him like I used to do behind Ella, or even with Dinah Washington when she was with the (inaudible) band and I was with Hamp, you know.
